title: 'Many tears shed': Grant County staff member reacts to loss of Boys & Girls Club - NewsBreak
text:
MARION, Ind. (WANE) — Multiple sides are speaking out in the aftermath of Grant County losing its Boys & Girls Club chapter in late July. The organization made the announcement July 24, saying it would have to close the next day. The club is overseen by the Boys & Girls Clubs of Fort Wayne, which acts as a regional affiliate for Boys & Girls Clubs of America. President and CEO Joe Jordan told WANE 15 the Fort Wayne branch took over operations in Grant County around five years ago because the national brass threatened to end the club due to a lack of programs and community support. He added that a “major stakeholder” in the Grant County community will try to fill the gap and provide some after-school programs for children. However, a staff member at the Grant County branch argues that there was enough community support to keep the club afloat and that mismanagement from Fort Wayne led to its downfall. Necole Pfeiffer, director of programs for Boys & Girls Club of Grant County, responded to WANE 15 Tuesday morning after an interview request and said believes the organization did get enough support from the local community. [Joe Jordan] claimed we were not running programming and we did not have community support! I feel like that is far from the truth! We were running programming successfully as well as making community partnerships. He never put the word out to the community that we needed the help he says we needed! He gave our board until Aug. 1 to raise $90,000 … we did that! Then they claimed it was not enough. I just received an email a few days ago that we received $20,000 from Taco Bell for a grant. So, we were making the money! Joe Jordan lost us our $60,000 grant from United Way by talking about Fort Wayne when they wanted to hear from us in Grant County. This was the second year in a row! Critical funding was lost to Grant County at the hands of Joe Jordan. This closure has had a tremendous impact on our community. Fort Wayne has multiple sites up and running. The Boys & Girls Club of Grant County was all we had for our community to turn to as their affordable safe place for their children after school. This is devastating to Grant County! We have had so many people reach out to us telling us had they knew we were in such dire need they would have provided the funding … but we were only given 24 hours between the meeting telling us we were closed and the time our doors were no longer allowed to be opened to the public! We have had many tears shed due to the loss of the club. They say they that they are turning it over to a trusted partner of the community but NOTHING will be the same as what we as stuff of the club will give these babies of Grant County. On Wednesday, Jordan responded to Pfeiffer’s statement: For the past five years, Boys & Girls Clubs of Northeast Indiana (BGCNEI) has proudly ensured that young people in Grant County received exceptional programming in a safe and supportive environment. While we are incredibly grateful for the opportunity to have served the youth and families of this community, our board of directors made the difficult decision to cease operations of the Grant County site, effective late July, due to ongoing financial challenges that compromised the Club’s long-term sustainability. However, our commitment to the children of Grant County remains unwavering. We are currently engaged in confidential discussions with another community partner, with the hope that they will assume operations and continue to provide quality afterschool programming once the school year begins. We sincerely thank all the community members who supported our efforts over the past several years and look forward to a continued positive impact for the youth of Grant County through this transition. United Way of Grant County also provided a statement to WANE 15 Wednesday that confirmed the organization did not provide funding to Boys & Girls Club of Grant County this year, but United Way said it did offer support in other ways: United Way of Grant County has proudly supported the Boys & Girls Club of Grant County in past years through our annual Community Investment process, which directs funding to specific programs that address local needs. Each year, nonprofit organizations are invited to apply for program-based grants. These applications are reviewed by a volunteer committee of Grant County residents who make thoughtful funding recommendations based on community priorities and available resources. Final decisions are approved by our Board of Directors.
As a matter of policy, United Way does not fund agencies in full. We invest in specific, vetted programs that are designed to meet pressing local needs. This ensures accountability, impact, and alignment with our community’s highest priorities. On average, our grants range from $10,000 to $40,000 and typically represent just a portion of an organization’s overall budget. We work with many valued community partners, and this past year’s funding cycle was especially competitive. While the Boys & Girls Club of Grant County was not selected for program funding in this annual grant cycle, we expressed our commitment to their organization through other avenues of support including professional development, volunteer engagement, marketing, and networking opportunities.
We were not informed in advance of the decision to close the Grant County club. Like many in our community, we were saddened to learn of its sudden closure just days before the school year began. Our hearts go out to the children, families, and staff members affected by this unexpected change. It is unclear when the “major stakeholder” intends to announce their plan for the successor to Boys & Girls Club of Grant County. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WANE 15.
